Let

\[
E=x^{7}(yz-1)+y^{7}(zx-1)+z^{7}(xy-1).
\]

Using the condition \(x+y+z=xyz\), we have

\[
x(yz-1)=y+z,
\]

and cyclically. Therefore

\[
x^{7}(yz-1)=x^6(y+z),
\]

so

\[
E=x^6(y+z)+y^6(z+x)+z^6(x+y).
\]

Expanding,

\[
E=x^6y+x^6z+y^6z+y^6x+z^6x+z^6y.
\]

Now apply AM-GM to these six positive terms:

\[
E\ge 6\sqrt[6]{(x^6y)(x^6z)(y^6z)(y^6x)(z^6x)(z^6y)}.
\]

The product inside the root is

\[
x^{14}y^{14}z^{14}=(xyz)^{14}.
\]

Hence

\[
E\ge 6(xyz)^{14/6}=6(xyz)^{7/3}.
\]

Let \(p=xyz\). Since \(x+y+z=xyz\), we have \(p=x+y+z\). By AM-GM,

\[
p=x+y+z\ge 3\sqrt[3]{xyz}=3p^{1/3}.
\]

Because \(p>0\), this gives

\[
p^{2/3}\ge 3,
\]

so

\[
p\ge 3\sqrt3.
\]

Therefore,

\[
E\ge 6(3\sqrt3)^{7/3}.
\]

Compute:

\[
(3\sqrt3)^{7/3}=(3^{3/2})^{7/3}=3^{7/2}=27\sqrt3.
\]

Thus

\[
E\ge 6\cdot 27\sqrt3=162\sqrt3.
\]

Equality holds when \(x=y=z\). From \(x+y+z=xyz\), we get

\[
3x=x^3 \implies x^2=3 \implies x=\sqrt3.
\]

At \(x=y=z=\sqrt3\),

\[
E=3(\sqrt3)^7(3-1)=3\cdot 27\sqrt3\cdot 2=162\sqrt3.
\]

Hence the minimum value is

\[
\boxed{162\sqrt3}.
\]
